subject: english
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e. **'Species'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word to fill in blank number 1 is option 3:** "species".**
 
• The term **"species"** is used in biological taxonomy and is the basic unit of classification.
 
• **It refers** to a group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding.
 
• **In this context,** it correctly refers to different types of rats that have been identified and classified. The Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS) is an American partnership of federal agencies designed to provide consistent and reliable information on the taxonomy of biological species.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* 'According to the Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS) there are more than 60 **species** of rat, which means they come in all sizes. They are (2) ________ 5 inches (12 centimeters), or longer, according to Encyclopedia Britannica. The largest species is the Bosavi woolly rat, which was (3)______ in 2009 in the rainforest of Papua New Guinea (and doesn't have a scientific name yet). It is (4)_____ the size of a cat - 32.2 inches (82 cm) from nose to tail and (5)______ around 3.3 lbs. (1.5 kilograms), according to CNN.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options don't fit as well in this context:
 
 
• **"Entities" **- this is a very broad term that can refer to anything that exists, whether it be a physical object, a concept, or a fact. It is too vague to be used in the specific biological context of different types of rats.
 
• **"Sections" -** this term is more typically used to refer to parts of a physical object or divisions within an organization or piece of writing. It's not used to refer to types of living organisms.
 
• **"Objects" **- this term usually refers to inanimate physical things, not living organisms.
